in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **How many children are you asking about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm asking about one child - my daughter Alex. She's 15 and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You have a 15-year-old daughter named Alex who lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask: **Are you responsible for Alex's care, meaning you're providing for her needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for her care - I provide everything she needs like food, clothes, and a home. She lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency status: **Do you normally live in the UK? And if you were born outside the UK or are an EU/EEA/Swiss national, what is your immigration or residency status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I was born here, so there's no immigration status to worry about - I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, and is she living with you at home (rather than being in hospital, care, or any other residential accommodation for extended periods)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me. She's not in hospital or care or anything like that. She's 15, so she's still at school doing her GCSEs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her. It's just me caring for her.

**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your daughter Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 15 years old (under the age threshold of 16)
- She lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for her care and provide for all her needs
- You're a British citizen who normally lives in the UK
- Alex is in full-time education (doing her GCSEs)
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her

All the eligibility requirements are satisfied, so you should be able to successfully apply for Child Benefit.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit if you wish.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
